claims.rationale: Python conflates inheritance and interface-implementation syntactically; surfacing the distinction preserves cross-language consistency with TypeScript and avoids architectural lossiness
claims.excerpt: The adapter surfaces the distinction by routing Protocol bases to `implements` and everything else to `extends`

claims.claim: Adapter targets Python 3.12+ (supports PEP 695 `type` statement); older Python code still parses and indexes without special-case paths
claims.rationale: Defines the target Python version
claims.excerpt: Adapter targets Python 3.12+ (PEP 695 `type` statement supported). Older Python code parses and indexes fine; no special-case paths.

claims.claim: Adapter walks the project root during initialize and opens every .py file because Pyright performs no automatic cross-file analysis
claims.rationale: findReferences only returns hits in files seen via didOpen; warmup required
claims.excerpt: Adapter walks the project root during `initialize` and opens every `.py` file, mirroring TypeScriptAdapter's tsserver warmup.

claims.claim: Adapter's extensions list is [".py"] only; stub files (.pyi) are not indexed in v0.1
claims.rationale: Indexing stubs alongside source would produce duplicate atlas entries with distinct file_sha values and no consumer-visible link
claims.excerpt: The adapter's `extensions` list is `[".py"]`. **Stub files (`.pyi`) are not indexed in v0.1.**

claims.claim: Class signatures are constructed from source declaration rather than hover; hover is used only for method/function/type-alias/constant signatures
claims.rationale: Pyright hover for classes omits base classes and declaration header
claims.excerpt: Class signatures constructed from source declaration instead (`class Widget(Shape, Serializable):`)

claims.claim: Decorators (@property, @classmethod, @staticmethod, @dataclass, @runtime_checkable) appear in the signature string but do not influence SymbolKind
claims.rationale: Avoids commitment to caller interpretation; granularity gated on benchmark evidence
claims.excerpt: appear in the signature string when present (hover already includes them) but don't influence kind

claims.claim: Dynamic class construction (type(), dataclass-factory functions, metaclass-driven instantiation) is invisible to the adapter, mirroring Pyright's static-analysis limits
claims.rationale: Adapter is bounded by what Pyright surfaces as documentSymbols
claims.excerpt: Classes created via `type()` at runtime, dataclass-factory functions, or metaclass-driven instantiation aren't in Pyright's document symbols and therefore aren't in the atlas.

claims.claim: Import alias tracing is localized to the file's top-level imports; no whole-module import graph walk
claims.rationale: Keeps mechanism bounded and avoids expensive graph traversal
claims.excerpt: Parsing is localized to the file's top-level imports; no whole-module import graph walk.

claims.claim: Pathological class-header inputs (function-call bases, Optional[Bar] base, star-unpacked bases, dynamically-constructed classes) degrade to fewer bases extracted rather than wrong data
claims.rationale: Documents intentional degradation behavior so future readers don't treat as bugs
claims.excerpt: Wrong routing (a real base dropped) is possible in pathological inputs but never wrong data (an extracted base that isn't one).

claims.claim: Protocol detection uses three composed mechanisms: (a) hardcoded canonical names, (b) per-file import alias tracing, (c) symbol-inventory lookup for project-defined Protocols; disjunction is inclusive
claims.rationale: No single mechanism covers all cases; each is independently valuable and testable
claims.excerpt: at lookup time, a base name is treated as a Protocol if ANY of the three mechanisms fires

claims.claim: Pyright 1.1.409+ is the sole Python LSP backend for v0.1, listed as non-optional in peerDependencies + devDependencies
claims.rationale: Pyright is Microsoft-maintained with broadest MCP-client ecosystem familiarity; alternatives fail capability requirements
claims.excerpt: **Pyright 1.1.409+** is the sole Python LSP backend for v0.1. Listed in `peerDependencies` + `devDependencies` as non-optional

claims.claim: async def surfaces in the signature string only; no separate kind or claim-extraction pass for async
claims.rationale: Async/await signal extraction is post-MVP
claims.excerpt: `async def` surfaces in the signature string. No separate kind, no separate claim-extraction pass.

claims.claim: textDocument/implementation is unavailable in Pyright; usedByTypes must be computed via source declaration parsing during full-indexing; single-file queries without inventory return [] for usedByTypes
claims.rationale: Pyright returns JSON-RPC error -32601 for implementation requests; adapter must work around this
claims.excerpt: **Source declaration parsing** computes `usedByTypes` during full-indexing runs. Single-file queries that don't have inventory context return `[]` for `usedByTypes`.

claims.claim: v0.1 surfaces one symbol per overloaded name with the first overload's signature; full overload set is invisible at atlas layer
claims.rationale: Pyright collapses @overload entries to a single documentSymbol; limitation accepted for v0.1
claims.excerpt: v0.1 surfaces one symbol per overloaded name with the first overload's signature. Limitation documented below.

claims.claim: Declaration-header parser scope is restricted to the class Name(Base1, Base2): pattern and common variants; does not handle general Python expressions
claims.rationale: Bounded surface area keeps the parser ~50 LOC and unit-testable
claims.excerpt: Scope is deliberately narrow — the supported surface is the `class Name(Base1, Base2):` pattern and its common variants.

claims.claim: Parser does not resolve qualified names, does not evaluate base-list expressions, and does not handle PEP 695 generic class syntax specially (read past transparently via selectionRange)
claims.rationale: Explicit non-capabilities of the parser, with degradation behavior
claims.excerpt: Does not execute or evaluate base-list expressions. A base-list computed from a function call ... degrades to "bases not extracted"

claims.claim: Parser locates declaration via documentSymbol.selectionRange.start.line so decorators on preceding lines are ignored
claims.rationale: selectionRange points at the identifier, sidestepping decorator handling
claims.excerpt: Use `documentSymbol.selectionRange.start.line` to find the `class <Name>` token. `selectionRange` points at the identifier, so decorators on preceding lines ... don't affect this step

claims.claim: Parser strips balanced [...] spans (generic parameter lists), splits on commas at depth zero, drops name=... kwargs, and strips trailing [...] from each surviving token; dotted names preserved intact
claims.rationale: Defines the exact extraction rules for base classes
claims.excerpt: Strip trailing `[...]` from each surviving token. A base like `Base1[str]` becomes `Base1`. Dotted names (`typing.Protocol`, `collections.abc.Mapping`) are preserved intact as single tokens

claims.claim: Parser tracks paren depth across newlines to read multi-line bases spans as a single span
claims.rationale: Multi-line class declarations are common; must be handled correctly
claims.excerpt: are read as a single bases span by tracking paren depth across lines until depth returns to zero.

claims.claim: ADR-07 TypeInfo.{extends, implements, usedByTypes} semantics hold identically across TypeScript and Python adapters; only extraction mechanism differs
claims.rationale: Cross-adapter contract consistency
claims.excerpt: `TypeInfo.{extends, implements, usedByTypes}` has the same meaning in both adapters; only the extraction mechanism differs.

claims.claim: A single workspaceFolders initialize call covering the module root is sufficient for cross-package implementation indexing; no per-package reinitialize.
claims.rationale: Empirically verified during probe: cross-package implementers surfaced once files were opened alongside root-package files.
claims.excerpt: A single `workspaceFolders` initialize call covering the module root is sufficient for gopls to index implementation relationships across all packages in the workspace.

claims.claim: Adapter flattens interface methods from gopls's nested children into top-level Symbol records with dot-encoded names (e.g., `Shape.Area`).
claims.rationale: Flat layout matches struct-method shape and keeps the downstream claim-extraction pipeline uniform.
claims.excerpt: the adapter flattens interface children to top-level Symbol records

claims.claim: Adapter outputs reduced symbol kinds (function, method, class, interface, other); struct and type-definition collapse to `class`.
claims.rationale: Per ADR-01's symbol-kind reduction.
claims.excerpt: the adapter outputs reduced kinds: `function`, `method`, `class`, `interface`, `other`

claims.claim: Flattened interface-method Symbol records must carry a `parent_id` field pointing to the interface's SymbolId.
claims.rationale: Flattening without the back-pointer would drop the interface-membership signal entirely; parent_id is the authoritative link, dot-in-name is convenience.
claims.excerpt: the flattened method Symbol records a `parent_id` field pointing to the interface's SymbolId... Flattening without the back-pointer would drop the interface-membership signal entirely

claims.claim: For embedded structs, adapter preserves the embedded-field documentSymbol shape (B as a kind:8 field of A); promoted method tracking happens via getTypeInfo, not listSymbols.
claims.rationale: Attempting to synthesize phantom method-child entries is out of scope; promoted methods surface via implementation+hover.
claims.excerpt: the adapter preserves the embedded-field documentSymbol shape for ingestion... Attempting to synthesize phantom method-child entries is out of scope.

claims.claim: Generic type-parameter lists are preserved verbatim in signatures, names, and SymbolIds; no adapter-side reconstruction or normalization.
claims.rationale: The type-parameter list is part of the canonical name.
claims.excerpt: signatures, names, and SymbolIds carry generics verbatim. No adapter-side reconstruction or normalization.

claims.claim: GoAdapter must ensure the `go` binary is on the gopls process's PATH and validate via `go version` preflight, emitting an actionable error on failure.
claims.rationale: Without `go` on PATH, gopls emits 'no views' and returns no symbols; this requirement is gopls-specific and must not be inherited from generic LspClient defaults.
claims.excerpt: Gopls spawns `go` as a subprocess for module loading... **Adapter responsibility:** document `go` as a user PATH requirement... On initialization, validate by running `go version` as a preflight

claims.claim: GoAdapter must implement a `workspace/configuration` handler that returns a length-matched array of objects, not a null stub.
claims.rationale: Gopls does not tolerate null responses to workspace/configuration (unlike pyright); null causes the same 'no views' cascade as missing PATH.
claims.excerpt: implement this handler, do not delegate to a generic null-stub

claims.claim: GoAdapter.initialize() blocks on a waitForServerReady race against a 3s ceiling, absorbing gopls cold-start at init time so getDiagnostics tightens to a 1500ms per-call ceiling.
claims.rationale: Gopls fires $/progress on initialized; ADR-18 cross-cutting readiness pattern applies.
claims.excerpt: The adapter's `initialize()` blocks on a `waitForServerReady` race against a 3s ceiling so init returns when the workspace is loaded

claims.claim: Gopls is user-installed via `go install`, not bundled as a peerDependency; follows the tsserver pattern of user-provided, PATH-resolved binaries.
claims.rationale: Gopls is Go-distributed and cannot be a npm peerDependency like pyright.
claims.excerpt: gopls is Go-distributed: users install via `go install golang.org/x/tools/gopls@<version>`

claims.claim: Gopls v0.21.1+ is the sole Go LSP backend for v0.1; alternatives (manual go/parser+go/types, go-langserver, govim wrappers) are rejected.
claims.rationale: Gopls already solves cross-package resolution, interface satisfaction, and generics inference; alternatives are unmaintained or duplicate gopls's machinery.
claims.excerpt: **Gopls v0.21.1+** is the sole Go LSP backend for v0.1.

claims.claim: Gopls version pin must track the Go toolchain version closely; a stale gopls pinned against a newer Go toolchain silently breaks module loading.
claims.rationale: Gopls's 'only latest Go' build-support policy means cross-version incompatibility (e.g., v0.16 incompatible with Go 1.26).
claims.excerpt: Pin must track the Go toolchain version closely — gopls's "only latest Go" build-support policy means a gopls compiled against Go 1.23 cannot be used against a Go 1.26 toolchain.

claims.claim: Iota const block members are flattened to independent top-level Symbol records; do not reconstruct a synthetic block container.
claims.rationale: Matches gopls's native shape; iota is syntactic sugar; block membership is recoverable from line-adjacency if needed.
claims.excerpt: flatten iota const members to independent top-level Symbol records. Do NOT reconstruct a synthetic block container.

claims.claim: Preserve gopls's receiver-encoded method names verbatim in SymbolId (e.g., `(*Rectangle).Area`); do not strip parens or receiver prefix.
claims.rationale: Receiver encoding is deterministic, unique per-file, and carries pointer-vs-value semantic information that would otherwise need a side-field; multiple types in one file may share method names.
claims.excerpt: preserve the gopls receiver-encoded name verbatim in SymbolId. Do NOT strip parens or receiver prefix.

claims.claim: Vendor mode, cgo, and //go:generate semantics are not specifically handled; generated files indexed as-is, generator comments opaque.
claims.rationale: Unprobed areas treated as best-effort; not target use cases for v0.1.
claims.excerpt: **No vendor-mode special-casing.**... **No cgo support.**... **No `//go:generate` semantics.**

claims.claim: getTypeInfo calls `textDocument/implementation` once and partitions results into `implements` vs `usedByTypes`; `extends` is derived from hover or documentSymbol children. No inventory-walk fallback.
claims.rationale: Gopls's implementation endpoint surfaces both directions of interface satisfaction reliably, including cross-package; pyright's inventory-walk gap does not exist for gopls.
claims.excerpt: `getTypeInfo` calls `implementation` once, partitions results by whether each result location is an interface-type or concrete-type declaration

claims.claim: v0.1 Go adapter supports only single-module mode with one workspaceFolders root; no go.work workspaces, no multi-module, no GOPATH.
claims.rationale: v0.1 scoping limitation; v0.2+ if demand surfaces.
claims.excerpt: **Single-module only.** The v0.1 Go adapter does not support Go workspaces (`go.work`) or multi-module setups.

claims.claim: v0.1 Go adapter surfaces symbols from all `.go` files regardless of build tag; package-level dedup is the pipeline layer's responsibility, not the adapter's or claim-extraction's.
claims.rationale: Keeps the adapter contract clean ('surface everything gopls sees') and lets the pipeline apply language-specific semantics like build-tag dedup.
claims.excerpt: The v0.1 Go adapter does NOT filter by build tag... pipeline layer is responsible for package-level dedup.

claims.claim: Compact-format multi-symbol responses use delimiter line '--- get_symbol_context: <symbol> (N of M) ---' with the caller's input string verbatim.
claims.rationale: The delimiter encodes input identifier and positional context so consumers can map sub-bundles back to original inputs — load-bearing when partial failures break 1:1 correspondence.
claims.excerpt: Where `<symbol>` is the **caller's input string verbatim**, `N` is the 1-indexed position in the request, and `M` is the total batch size.

claims.claim: Dedup is exact-string-match with .trim() whitespace normalization, applied before resolution; case-sensitive; full SymbolId and plain name producing the same atlas entry are NOT deduped.
claims.rationale: Matches caller mental model (each input string is one ask) and aligns with case-sensitive symbol resolution from ADR-01; resolution-keyed dedup would complicate partial-failure rendering.
claims.excerpt: **Dedup is exact-string-match with `.trim()` whitespace normalization, applied before resolution.**

claims.claim: Disambiguation outcomes do not deduplicate; dedup applies to input strings only, not resolution outcomes.
claims.rationale: Preserves input-layer dedup semantics; two distinct inputs producing overlapping disambiguation candidates both render.
claims.excerpt: **Disambiguation does not deduplicate.** ... Dedup is applied to **input strings**, not to resolution outcomes.

claims.claim: Exceeding the symbol cap returns McpError InvalidParams (protocol-level error), not silent truncation.
claims.rationale: A cap violation is the caller using the API wrong, structurally distinct from per-symbol resolution failure; silent truncation is a contract hazard.
claims.excerpt: **Cap exceedance returns `McpError` (protocol-level).** When the caller sends 11+ items, the response is a JSON-RPC `InvalidParams` error

claims.claim: Existing single-symbol golden-output tests must pass byte-identical after multi-symbol implementation; any divergence blocks Step 4 ship.
claims.rationale: Makes backward compatibility a verifiable test criterion rather than a claimed property.
claims.excerpt: Any divergence in single-string output indicates regression and blocks Step 4 ship.

claims.claim: Extend the existing get_symbol_context tool to accept string or string[]; do not add a new multi-symbol tool.
claims.rationale: MCP tool selection is by name; oneOf schemas are supported, and the three-primitive framing in CLAUDE.md is load-bearing. Adding a fourth tool inflates per-call context cost without a new mental category.
claims.excerpt: The existing `get_symbol_context` tool is extended to accept either a single string or a string array. **No new tool is added.**

claims.claim: Handler normalizes single string to a length-1 array internally, then fans out the existing resolve → buildBundle → render path per item with shared options.
claims.rationale: Describes the implementation refactor in src/mcp/handlers/get-symbol-context.ts.
claims.excerpt: `parseArgs` learns to accept array input, normalizes to a `string[]` internal shape (single string → length-1 array), then fans out the existing per-symbol path

claims.claim: JSON-format multi-symbol responses use a {results: [{symbol, bundle, error}]} envelope where each entry has exactly one of bundle or error.
claims.rationale: Symmetric success/failure shape simplifies consumer code walking the array.
claims.excerpt: Each entry has the caller's input string verbatim, plus exactly one of `bundle` (on success) or `error` (on per-symbol failure).

claims.claim: No atlas schema, extraction pipeline, or storage change; this is purely a query-time API surface change.
claims.rationale: Scopes the change strictly to MCP query-time surface.
claims.excerpt: **No atlas schema change.** This is purely a query-time API surface change.

claims.claim: No server-side warning is emitted for pathologically large batches; bundle-size and token-budget management is the caller's concern via max_refs.
claims.rationale: 10 symbols × deep depth × default max_refs can exceed model context windows; the server does not police this.
claims.excerpt: No server-side warning is emitted.

claims.claim: Options (depth, include, max_refs, file_hint, format) apply uniformly across all symbols in a batch; no per-symbol overrides.
claims.rationale: YAGNI — c4 use case doesn't need heterogeneity; per-symbol overrides would break the clean string | string[] extension.
claims.excerpt: `depth`, `include`, `max_refs`, `file_hint`, and `format` apply **uniformly across all symbols in the batch.**

claims.claim: Per-symbol failures are inlined as ERR sub-bundles; whole-call isError:true is set only when every symbol in the batch failed.
claims.rationale: Whole-call isError on any failure defeats the c4 use case (one typo invalidating four good bundles), making multi-symbol a strictly weaker substitute for regex-OR Grep.
claims.excerpt: **Whole-call `isError: true` is set only when EVERY symbol in the batch failed to resolve.**

claims.claim: Response order matches request order; no reordering by relevance, language, or success status.
claims.rationale: get_symbol_context is the 'I already know what I want' primitive; relevance ranking is find_by_intent's job.
claims.excerpt: **Response order matches request order.** ... **No reordering by relevance, language, or success status.**

claims.claim: Schema in src/mcp/schemas.ts gains oneOf:[string, array] for the symbol property, with the cap exported as MAX_SYMBOLS_PER_CALL.
claims.rationale: Documents the concrete code change required by the contract.
claims.excerpt: `symbol` property gains `oneOf: [string, array]` shape. ... Cap exposed as `MAX_SYMBOLS_PER_CALL` exported constant.

claims.claim: The compact-format delimiter '--- get_symbol_context: <symbol> (N of M) ---' is part of the wire contract and cannot change without breaking consumer parsers.
claims.rationale: Future refinements to the delimiter require a DESIGN.md amendment plus ADR addendum.
claims.excerpt: The `--- get_symbol_context: <symbol> (N of M) ---` format cannot change without breaking consumer parsers.

claims.claim: When all symbols fail, the isError:true body starts with 'ERR all_symbols_failed\n  COUNT <N>' followed by per-symbol ERR sub-bundles.
claims.rationale: Lets consumers detect complete failure from isError without parsing the body, and extract per-symbol detail when needed.
claims.excerpt: Format: `ERR all_symbols_failed\n  COUNT <N>\n` followed by the standard delimiter-and-sub-bundle shape.

claims.claim: When file_hint is provided with a multi-symbol input, it applies to every name resolution in the batch.
claims.rationale: Supports the use case where all batched symbols share a directory; callers needing different hints must split calls or use full SymbolIds.
claims.excerpt: When `file_hint` is provided alongside a multi-symbol input, it applies to every name resolution.

claims.claim: When symbol is a string (not array), response shape is the legacy single-bundle shape (no delimiter, no results envelope); detection is by input shape, not response.
claims.rationale: Preserves byte-level backward compatibility for every existing single-symbol caller.
claims.excerpt: This preserves byte-level backward compatibility for every existing caller.

claims.claim: disambiguation_required and no_adapter failures in a batch are rendered per-symbol in the positional slot; siblings render normally and the call does not abort.
claims.rationale: Consistent with partial-failure semantics: resolution failures are per-symbol, not whole-call.
claims.excerpt: the disambiguation block is rendered **in that symbol's positional slot only**. Sibling symbols continue to render their bundles or their own ERR blocks normally; the call does not abort.

claims.claim: find_by_intent remains single-query in v0.3; multi-query find_by_intent is out of scope.
claims.rationale: Batched intent queries have their own ranking and dedup design problems deferred from this ADR.
claims.excerpt: **`find_by_intent` is unchanged in v0.3.** Multi-query `find_by_intent` is a separate concern.

claims.claim: impact_of_change remains single-symbol in v0.3; multi-symbol blast-radius semantics is explicitly deferred.
claims.rationale: Multi-symbol blast-radius (set-union vs per-symbol, ranking, ref dedup) is a separate design problem.
claims.excerpt: **`impact_of_change` is unchanged in v0.3.** ... is explicitly deferred. Non-goals.

claims.claim: Maximum 10 symbols per call (MAX_SYMBOLS_PER_CALL = 10).
claims.rationale: Phase 7 c4 used 3 symbols; 10 provides ~3× headroom while keeping bundle size predictable.
claims.excerpt: **Maximum 10 symbols per call** (`MAX_SYMBOLS_PER_CALL = 10`).

claims.claim: Doctor check `atlas.bm25_recommendation` emits one of four outcomes based on 2×2 matrix of flag-state × atlas-density; 'dense' = any symbol carrying ≥6 attached claims
claims.rationale: At ≤5 attached claims top-5 surfaces all of them so reorder is invisible; at 6+ ranking choice becomes user-visible
claims.excerpt: "Dense" is defined as any symbol in the atlas carrying ≥6 claims attached

claims.claim: Cross-symbol BM25 ranking is find_by_intent's territory, not extended in get_symbol_context
claims.rationale: BM25 path here scores only claims attached to a single symbol
claims.excerpt: Single-symbol claims subset only. This BM25 path scores claims attached to a single symbol. Cross-symbol BM25 ranking ... is `find_by_intent`'s territory, not extended here.

claims.claim: Cycle-observation 19: when shipping mechanically-functional capability with caller-activation as separate concern, add an activation verification check to the next cycle's measurement entry-points
claims.rationale: Documentation of activation gap is necessary but not sufficient; without verification, capability can remain dormant across cycles
claims.excerpt: Add an activation verification to the next cycle's measurement entry-points.

claims.claim: Embedding-based ranking is explicitly deferred to v0.4+; this ADR uses FTS5 BM25 exclusively
claims.rationale: Per ADR-09 + DESIGN.md 'don't embed' rule
claims.excerpt: Embedding-based ranking. Explicitly deferred to v0.4+ per ADR-09 + DESIGN.md "don't embed" rule.

claims.claim: New `mcp` config section is established; future MCP-server query-time knobs land in the same section
claims.rationale: Provides a stable location for future query-time configuration
claims.excerpt: New `mcp` config section established here; future MCP-server query-time knobs land in the same section.

claims.claim: No name-overlap tiebreaker in get_symbol_context's BM25 chain (departure from ADR-09)
claims.rationale: All claims belong to a single symbol so name-overlap is degenerate; ADR-09 needs it because find_by_intent ranks multiple symbols
claims.excerpt: No name-overlap tiebreaker (departure from ADR-09's chain). In `get_symbol_context`, all claims belong to a single symbol

claims.claim: Non-matching claims sort to end via POSITIVE_INFINITY sentinel rather than being filtered out
claims.rationale: get_symbol_context's contract is 'give me everything,' not 'give me the relevant subset'; filtering is find_by_intent's job
claims.excerpt: POSITIVE_INFINITY sentinel for unmatched claims. Preserves the rule "all claims attached to the symbol surface in the bundle"

claims.claim: Quality-axis measurement (whether BM25-reordered bundles produce better Claude responses) is deferred to v0.9+; Ship 4a measured ordering shift only
claims.rationale: Activation→quality evidence loop remains open; candidate for v0.9+ extension
claims.excerpt: the downstream-task-quality consequence is empirically untested at this cycle. Worth v0.9+ candidate

claims.claim: Query string is caller-provided via optional `query` parameter; server-derived query synthesis was rejected
claims.rationale: Server-derived queries are design-debate territory; caller-provided matches find_by_intent precedent and preserves ADR-02's no-query-time-LLM rule
claims.excerpt: Rejected alternative — server-derived query. Synthesizing a query from the symbol name + nearby symbols + path tokens was considered. Rejected

claims.claim: Server flag `mcp.symbol_context_bm25` defaults to false; two-layer gating originally required both flag-on AND caller query for BM25 activation
claims.rationale: Default-off preserves v0.2 baseline byte-equivalence regardless of how query parameters propagate
claims.excerpt: A new config field `mcp.symbol_context_bm25: boolean` controls whether the BM25 path is available at all. Defaults to `false` (v0.2 baseline preserved).

claims.claim: Tiebreaker chain α when query+flag active: BM25 ASC → Severity → Source alphabetical → Claim id ASC; BM25 dominates rather than acting as in-severity tiebreaker
claims.rationale: Severity-first ordering (alternative β) preserves exactly the broken ranking Phase 6 §5.1 documented, since all 17 ADR-05 claims tie on severity=hard
claims.excerpt: Tiebreaker chain α — BM25 dominates when query provided

claims.claim: Users preferring severity-first triage ordering should leave mcp.symbol_context_bm25 at its default (false); enabling materially changes top-N for densely-attached symbols
claims.rationale: Neither ordering is universally better — they optimize for different reading patterns
claims.excerpt: Users who prefer severity-first ordering should leave the flag at its default (`false`).

claims.claim: When called with multi-symbol input, the `query` parameter applies uniformly to every symbol in the batch; no per-symbol overrides
claims.rationale: Matches ADR-15 §3's uniform-per-symbol-options rule
claims.excerpt: the `query` parameter applies uniformly to every symbol in the batch. No per-symbol query overrides.

claims.claim: get_symbol_context extends ADR-09's BM25 ranking primitive, gated behind an optional caller-provided query parameter
claims.rationale: Addresses Gap 2 (non-query-aware ranking) and Gap 3 (tool asymmetry) identified in Phase 6 §5.1 mechanism analysis
claims.excerpt: This ADR addresses Gap 2 + Gap 3 directly by extending ADR-09's BM25 ranking primitive from `find_by_intent` to `get_symbol_context`'s intent block, gated behind an optional caller-provided query parameter.

claims.claim: v0.8 Step 1 amendment: handler moved from two-layer gating to server-flag-only gating with symbol-name synthesis fallback (bm25Query = args.query ?? symbol.name)
claims.rationale: Closes the v0.3-era activation gap by moving activation responsibility from caller to handler
claims.excerpt: post-v0.8 Step 1 — server-flag-only, synth fallback ...(deps.symbolContextBM25 === true ? { bm25Query: args.query ?? symbol.name } : {})

claims.claim: Degenerate symbol names (punctuation-only) reduce to empty tokens; sortClaimsByBM25 falls through to sortClaimsBySeverityThenSource, gracefully degrading to v0.2 ordering
claims.rationale: Synthesis must handle FTS5 unicode61 tokenizer edge cases without errors
claims.excerpt: Net effect: degenerate-name synthesis degrades gracefully to v0.2 ordering within that symbol's slot.

claims.claim: Reuse ADR-09's exported BM25 primitives (sanitizeQuery, buildMatchQuery) from find-by-intent.ts to keep semantics aligned across tools
claims.rationale: Minimizes implementation surface and keeps both tools' BM25 semantics aligned
claims.excerpt: `sanitizeQuery` and `buildMatchQuery` are already exported from `src/queries/find-by-intent.ts`. The BM25 SQL is a small variant of the existing find_by_intent query

claims.claim: Two ship-blocker canary tests protect backward compatibility: bm25Query absent → byte-identical to v0.2; bm25Query present → BM25 reorders. Future readers must not weaken these assertions during refactors
claims.rationale: Forms a 3-data-point pattern across v0.3 work paralleling ADR-15 and Step 5 canaries
claims.excerpt: future readers MUST NOT weaken these assertions during refactors

claims.claim: camelCase splitting is not implemented; v0.4+ candidate only if benchmarks reveal users expect queries like 'lsp client' to match LspClient.
claims.rationale: No empirical signal currently justifies expanding the surface.
claims.excerpt: Not required by the bug and not driven by dogfood evidence.

claims.claim: Each indexed text column (claim, rationale, excerpt) is stored twice: original form plus a copy with '_' and '-' replaced by spaces, concatenated.
claims.rationale: Tokenizer change alone would regress natural-language queries; dual-form indexing preserves both identifier and component-word matching.
claims.excerpt: Migration v5 fixes this by indexing each text column **twice**, once in the original form and once with `_` and `-` replaced by spaces, concatenated

claims.claim: FTS5 claims_fts virtual table uses unicode61 tokenizer with tokenchars '_-' so underscore and hyphen are token characters, not separators.
claims.rationale: Identifier-shaped queries like narrow_attribution and find-by-intent must index as single tokens to avoid silent search misses.
claims.excerpt: tokenize="unicode61 tokenchars '_-'"

claims.claim: Index size grows approximately 2× on text columns due to dual-form indexing; acceptable because claims are short (median under 200 chars).
claims.rationale: Quantifies the storage cost trade-off accepted by the design.
claims.excerpt: Index size grows ~2× on text columns.

claims.claim: Query-side expansion is not added to buildMatchQuery; indexed-side dual-form coverage is preferred over query-side identifier-expansion logic.
claims.rationale: Considered and rejected because dual-form indexing makes query expansion redundant and keeps buildMatchQuery small.
claims.excerpt: Query expansion in `buildMatchQuery`. Considered and rejected in favor of dual-form indexing.

claims.claim: The trigram tokenizer is rejected because it replaces BM25 ranking, indexes three-character substrings (larger index), and weakens phrase relevance.
claims.rationale: The bug is structural rather than lexical; trigram would regress canary cases ADR-09 validated.
claims.excerpt: trigram is a much bigger hammer than the problem requires and would regress the canary cases ADR-09 validated

claims.claim: buildMatchQuery wraps any token containing '-' in double quotes to defuse FTS5's AND-NOT operator interpretation of hyphens between barewords.
claims.rationale: Without quoting, queries like `find-by-intent` parse as `find NOT by NOT intent` and error with `no such column: by`.
claims.excerpt: FTS5's MATCH grammar treats `-` between two barewords as the AND-NOT operator

claims.claim: claims_fts uses content='claims' so dual-form expansion lives only in the FTS index; SELECTs return original verbatim text from the base claims table.
claims.rationale: Atlas round-trip must remain lossless per ADR-06; base claims table is the source of truth.
claims.excerpt: `content='claims'` is preserved, so the dual-form expansion lives only in the FTS index

claims.claim: find_by_intent remains a claims search; symbol-name search via FTS is explicitly out of scope.
claims.rationale: ADR-09's boundary is preserved; ADR-17 does not change it.
claims.excerpt: ADR-09 explicitly excludes this and ADR-17 does not change that boundary. `find_by_intent` remains a claims search.

claims.claim: get_symbol_context inherits the identifier-aware behavior automatically because sortClaimsByBM25 reuses sanitizeQuery and buildMatchQuery.
claims.rationale: Documents propagation of the fix to other consumers of the shared query helpers.
claims.excerpt: ADR-16's `sortClaimsByBM25` reuses ADR-09's `sanitizeQuery` and `buildMatchQuery` exports.

claims.claim: Tokens containing only '_' need no quoting in MATCH queries since FTS5 grammar has no special meaning for underscore.
claims.rationale: Explains scope of quoting logic — only hyphens require escaping.
claims.excerpt: Tokens containing only `_` need no quoting: FTS5 grammar has no special meaning for underscore.

claims.claim: sanitizeQuery regex is /[^\p{L}\p{N}\s_-]/gu, preserving '_' and '-' so identifier-shaped query tokens survive sanitization as single tokens.
claims.rationale: Query-side must preserve identifier characters to match the intact tokens now held in the index.
claims.excerpt: `sanitizeQuery` was changed from `/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s]/gu` to `/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s_-]/gu`

claims.claim: Schema migration v5 drops v2-era triggers and claims_fts, recreates the table with new tokenizer and dual-form triggers, and backfills from claims without touching the base table.
claims.rationale: Preserves external-content invariants and atlas.json round-trip while upgrading the FTS index.
claims.excerpt: Schema version bumps 4 → 5.

claims.claim: Adapter shutdown uses LSP shutdown request plus 2s timeout via LspClient.stop; shutdown-ready signal architecture is out of scope of this ADR.
claims.rationale: Explicitly listed as non-goal for B2.
claims.excerpt: Adapters use shutdown request + 2s timeout (`LspClient.stop`). Not in scope of B2.

claims.claim: BEGIN-title matching uses prefix-match (not exact match) to defend against ASCII vs U+2026 ellipsis variants without committing to a specific encoding.
claims.rationale: tsserver's title uses U+2026 horizontal ellipsis; prefix-match is defensive.
claims.excerpt: tsserver's title uses U+2026 horizontal ellipsis (`…`); prefix-match is defensive against ASCII variants without committing to a specific encoding.

claims.claim: Ceiling values (3s cold-start, 1.0s pyright per-call, 1.5s TS+gopls per-call) are empirical constants, not adaptive; adaptive per-repo ceilings are explicitly out of scope for v0.4.
claims.rationale: Derived from Step 1.1b probe + v0.3 observation; candidate for v0.5+ if benchmarks show constants inadequate.
claims.excerpt: Ceilings are constants; adaptive ceilings (e.g., per-repo priors from cost-tracking infrastructure) are out of scope for v0.4.

claims.claim: Future adapters (Rust, .NET v0.7+) should follow this pattern: write a per-adapter BEGIN matcher (~5 LOC) or opt out, wire waitForServerReady in initialize(), and replace inline diagnostic race with waitForDiagnostics.
claims.rationale: Helper file is shared infrastructure; pattern reuse keeps each per-server ADR scope focused.
claims.excerpt: Future adapters (Rust, .NET v0.7+) follow this pattern: write a per-adapter matcher (~5 LOC), wire `waitForServerReady` in `initialize()`, replace inline diagnostic race with `waitForDiagnostics` call.

claims.claim: Multi-workspace $/progress token disambiguation is deferred; v0.1 adapters assume single-workspace workspaceFolders.
claims.rationale: Multi-workspace deferred per ADR-14 Limitations.
claims.excerpt: v0.1 adapters use single-workspace `workspaceFolders`; multi-workspace deferred per ADR-14 §Limitations.

claims.claim: Title-match strings are hard-coded in upstream servers; upstream string changes would silently break server-readiness detection and fall back to ceiling.
claims.rationale: Acceptable per ceiling-as-safety-net framing; flagged so future readers revisit if servers upgrade.
claims.excerpt: Upstream string changes would silently break server-readiness detection and fall back to ceiling.

claims.claim: Diagnostic readiness must be split into two signals: server-readiness (cold-start, one-shot at initialize) and per-file readiness (per getDiagnostics call), rather than collapsed into a single per-call ceiling.
claims.rationale: Conflating them forces ceilings wide enough to absorb cold-start, slowing every warm call.
claims.excerpt: Conflating these into a single per-call ceiling forces the ceiling wide enough to absorb cold-start, slowing every warm call.

claims.claim: Shared helpers live in src/adapters/diagnostics-readiness.ts; adapter initialize() invokes waitForServerReady (tsserver/gopls only) and getDiagnostics() invokes waitForDiagnostics (all three adapters).
claims.rationale: Defines architectural boundary and integration points for the two-signal pattern.
claims.excerpt: Adapter `initialize()` invokes `waitForServerReady` | `typescript.ts`, `go.ts` | Block init until server-ready or ceiling

claims.claim: waitForDiagnostics resolves on the FIRST publishDiagnostics push for a URI and does not capture re-pushes; gopls re-pushing diagnostics for already-open files when new files open is a known staleness limitation.
claims.rationale: Caching-staleness consideration tracked for v0.5+.
claims.excerpt: `waitForDiagnostics` resolves on the FIRST `publishDiagnostics` push for a URI. Servers (notably gopls) sometimes re-push diagnostics for already-open files when new files open; the helper does not capture re-pushes.

claims.claim: waitForDiagnostics waits for the next textDocument/publishDiagnostics push for a given URI key with per-adapter ceilings: TypeScript 1500ms, Pyright 1000ms, gopls 1500ms.
claims.rationale: Ceilings derived from probe-observed warm-push times with headroom; pyright's ceiling absorbs its fast cold-start rather than using a separate init-time race.
claims.excerpt: `waitForDiagnostics` waits for the next `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` push for a given URI key, with a per-adapter ceiling that no longer needs to absorb cold-start

claims.claim: The TypeScript adapter must short-circuit waitForServerReady when the workspace has zero source files or lacks tsconfig.json/jsconfig.json, because tsserver won't emit project-load $/progress in those cases.
claims.rationale: tsserver fires $/progress BEGIN only after didOpen triggers project-load; without trigger or with loose-file mode, no signal will fire and the await would always hit the ceiling.
claims.excerpt: The TypeScript adapter applies two short-circuits to skip the `waitForServerReady` await when no `$/progress` flow could possibly fire

claims.claim: The helper must capture the $/progress token from a matching BEGIN and resolve only on END for that same token, because tsserver's END frame contains only {kind: "end"} with no title.
claims.rationale: Without token tracking, unrelated $/progress flows could accidentally satisfy the cold-start gate.
claims.excerpt: The helper captures the token from a matching BEGIN and resolves only on END for that same token, so unrelated `$/progress` flows can't accidentally satisfy the gate.

claims.claim: gopls does not apply short-circuits analogous to TypeScript's because gopls fires $/progress BEGIN immediately on initialized regardless of file-discovery, and the missing go.mod case is absorbed by the ceiling.
claims.rationale: Go modules have go.mod by definition; no-views cascade case is absorbed by ceiling.
claims.excerpt: gopls does NOT apply analogous short-circuits because gopls fires `$/progress` BEGIN immediately on `initialized` regardless of file-discovery

claims.claim: waitForServerReady is opt-in per adapter: tsserver and gopls wire it with per-server BEGIN matcher predicates; pyright opts out because pyright 1.1.409 emits no $/progress signal for analysis completion.
claims.rationale: Wrapping pyright in a no-op waitForServerReady would be honest-fiction code (an await against a never-matching predicate that always hits the ceiling).
claims.excerpt: The per-adapter opt-in is honest about per-server reality.

claims.claim: waitForServerReady races a $/progress END frame match against a 3-second ceiling that serves as a safety net for servers that don't emit a recognized signal.
claims.rationale: Typical cold-start completes in 0.5-1.2s; the ceiling fires only when the server doesn't emit a recognized signal.
claims.excerpt: The v0.4 helper `waitForServerReady` races a `$/progress` END frame match against a 3-second ceiling. The ceiling acts as a safety net

claims.claim: Adapter initialize() is now async-blocking on a real resource race for tsserver and gopls; callers depending on fast init may need to budget cold-start time.
claims.rationale: Cold-start cost shifts from first getDiagnostics call to initialize(); net session runtime similar or improved.
claims.excerpt: Adapter `initialize()` is now async-blocking on a real resource race, not just LSP `initialize` request roundtrip.

claims.claim: 'Distinguishable' column requires explicit caption framing: difference-of-means 95% CI excludes zero; effect-size + uncertainty only; not statistical significance
claims.rationale: Protects descriptive-CI-only commitment from being interpreted as NHST through the back door
claims.excerpt: Not a hypothesis test — explicit caption framing required

claims.claim: A/B randomization seed = SHA256(cell_id || trial_index || run_uuid)[:16]; manifest persisted to grading-run-manifest.json written before grading call; not visible to judge
claims.rationale: Deterministic seed allows post-hoc decode while keeping ordering hidden from judge
claims.excerpt: Manifest persisted to `grading-run-manifest.json` ... written before grading call; not visible to judge.

claims.claim: Anonymization strips entire trace, metrics, diagnostics, condition labels, bucket labels, target_symbol, repo, prompt_id, costs, wall_clock, written_at, and harness artifact filepaths from grading inputs
claims.rationale: Strip-list empirically derived from inspection of real Step 9 trial JSON; structural leakage requires whole-field stripping
claims.excerpt: Decision: strip the trace entirely. Strip-by-field is necessary but insufficient — the trace structure itself leaks.

claims.claim: Axis 4 (Hallucination) score-0 anchor uses a hypothetical-illustrative example because no real v0.3+v0.4 outputs produced score-0-level fabrication; this is disclosed transparently
claims.rationale: Transparency about anchor provenance protects peer-review defensibility
claims.excerpt: Disclosed transparently in `src/grading/rubric-prompt.ts` and in phase-9 reference doc.

claims.claim: Calls-Δ% is NOT used as a variance trigger; tokens-Δ is the load-bearing metric because calls is quantization noise on small-N cells
claims.rationale: Calls counts produce misleading percentages on small-N (e.g., 2→3 calls = 40%); calls-bucket reporting handles calls separately
claims.excerpt: Calls-Δ% NOT a variance trigger. ... calls is quantization noise on small-N cells

claims.claim: Compression from 4 axes to 3 (merging factual + hallucination) requires BOTH Spearman ≥ 0.85 AND fewer than 2 of 10 trials with >1-point gap; either alone preserves 4-axis separability
claims.rationale: Binding trigger preserves separability unless both empirical conditions hold
claims.excerpt: Both conditions must hold; either alone preserves 4-axis separability.

claims.claim: Cross-cell pooling reports fixed-effect at n=25; phase-9 ref doc must disclose that strict exchangeability is questionable given heterogeneous anchor cells
claims.rationale: Random-effects meta-analysis at k=5 has its own small-N problems; fixed-effect with disclosure is the v0.5 ship choice
claims.excerpt: Cross-cell pooling fixed-effect disclosure (phase-9 ref doc)

claims.claim: Cross-cutting methodology decisions (rubric, judge selection, anonymization, statistics, thresholds) are consolidated in this ADR; per-step ADRs reference back rather than relitigating
claims.rationale: Distributing methodology rationale across step files would scatter it and hurt peer-review reading
claims.excerpt: This ADR consolidates the cross-cutting pattern; per-step ADRs (if any) reference back to this one.

claims.claim: Cross-presentation-order check regrades k=5-10 of 25 pairs with A/B swapped via different seed; reported as Step 8 judge-agreement statistic
claims.rationale: Position-bias resistance verification
claims.excerpt: Cross-presentation-order check: for k=5-10 of the 25 pairs, regrade with A/B swapped via different seed.

claims.claim: Cross-vendor judge panel (Claude + GPT + Gemini) is deferred to v1.x post-launch hardening; out of v0.5 cost envelope
claims.rationale: Methodology limitation acknowledged as a non-goal for v0.5
claims.excerpt: Cross-vendor panel (Claude + GPT + Gemini) deferred to v1.x post-launch hardening per methodology limits

claims.claim: Default judge is Claude Sonnet 4.6; Opus 4.7 is the escalation backup if Step 6 calibration fails Travis-intuition correlation
claims.rationale: Single-judge with defined escalation; cross-vendor panel deferred to v1.x
claims.excerpt: Single-judge: Claude Sonnet 4.6 default; Opus 4.7 escalation backup if Step 6 calibration fails Travis-intuition correlation

claims.claim: Difference-of-means CI uses paired-t (df=n−1) on per-trial differences, not unpaired-pooled; cross-cell rollup applies paired-t at concatenated N=25 differences, not weighted-mean of per-cell differences
claims.rationale: v0.5 substrate is structurally paired; paired-t controls for trial-difficulty variance and is the textbook fit
claims.excerpt: Difference-of-means CI uses paired-t (per 2026-05-03 amendment). The v0.5 substrate is structurally paired

claims.claim: Direction agreement (sign-of-pair-difference agreement) is used over Spearman for small-N (n=3-5) per-axis substrate because Spearman at n=3 is binary in practice
claims.rationale: Direction agreement offers more granularity at small-N and catches mixed-pattern divergence aggregate Spearman can mask
claims.excerpt: Spearman at n=3 is binary in practice; direction agreement has more granularity at small-N.

claims.claim: Escalation fires when aggregate Spearman < 0.6 OR per-axis direction agreement < 75% on ≥1 of the 4 axes
claims.rationale: Defines explicit numeric thresholds for escalation
claims.excerpt: Escalation fires when at least one of the following conditions is breached

claims.claim: Filename-marker stripping preserves source-code file:line references (legitimate Axis 3 signal) but strips harness artifact filenames via mechanical regex with explicit source-extension allowlist (.py, .ts, .go, .rs, .java, .tsx, .js)
claims.rationale: Source file references are quality signal; harness filenames are leakage
claims.excerpt: Filename-marker stripping preserves source-code file:line references (legitimate Axis 3 quality signal ...); strips only harness artifact filenames

claims.claim: For trivial-lookup (trick-bucket) prompts, score actionability ≤ 1 if the answer buries the lookup in irrelevant ADR context
claims.rationale: Without this override, bloated-but-correct answers hide CA's over-extraction failure mode on trick-bucket prompts
claims.excerpt: Trick-bucket bloat handling (Axis 3 override): for trivial-lookup prompts ... score actionability ≤ 1

claims.claim: If escalation fires, Step 7-8 production runs on Opus (Option A) is the principled default; running production on a calibration-failed judge with disclosure does not survive peer-review scrutiny
claims.rationale: v0.5 thesis is methodology defensible under peer review
claims.excerpt: running production grading on a calibration-failed judge with disclosure (Option B) doesn't survive scrutiny.

claims.claim: Implementation specifics (e.g., rubric prompt text) live in source files following ADR-02 extraction-prompt single-source-of-truth precedent
claims.rationale: Methodology rationale at ADR layer, prompt text at source layer
claims.excerpt: per [ADR-02](ADR-02-extraction-sole-api-caller.md) extraction-prompt single-source-of-truth precedent

claims.claim: Judge ground-truth defaults to Option A (prompt + answer only); pivot to Option B (with inlined ADRs) requires factual-axis correlation < 0.6 AND other axes pass thresholds
claims.rationale: Pivot is reserved for the specific diagnostic case where factual axis is the lone underperformer; all-axes failure is a rubric-design problem instead
claims.excerpt: Pivot conjunction (binding at Step 6): switch to Option B IF Step 6 factual-axis correlation < 0.6 AND other axes pass thresholds.

claims.claim: Judge prompt includes anti-RLHF-bias instruction 'do not invent distinctions to break ties' to protect the tied-outputs pattern the rubric is designed to surface
claims.rationale: Tied-outputs surfacing is the rubric's primary purpose; judge tendency to over-call ties as wins would defeat it
claims.excerpt: The "do not invent distinctions to break ties" line is a deliberate anti-RLHF-bias instruction

claims.claim: MAD threshold of 1.5 for anchor refinement is empirically unanchored (set at half the scale range); first-cycle v0.5 calibration generates the empirical anchor for v0.6+
claims.rationale: Acknowledged limitation; subject to refinement in future cycles
claims.excerpt: MAD threshold at 1.5 for anchor refinement is empirically unanchored.

claims.claim: Mean Absolute Difference (MAD) > 1.5 triggers rubric anchor refinement, not escalation, when correlation is high
claims.rationale: Systematic offset with good correlation indicates rubric anchor problems, not judge-capability problems
claims.excerpt: MAD > 1.5: large systematic offset; trigger rubric anchor refinement (not escalation; if correlation is high, the rubric needs tighter anchors not a different judge).

claims.claim: No NHST, no p-values, no multiple-comparisons correction; reporting is descriptive CIs only
claims.rationale: At n=5 statistical power is too low for meaningful significance testing; descriptive framing avoids multiple-comparisons attack surface
claims.excerpt: No NHST; no p-values; no multiple-comparisons correction.

claims.claim: Once Step 7 production starts on a judge model, that model runs through Step 8 grading; no mid-cycle judge-model switching or per-cell judge selection
claims.rationale: Consistency of grading model across production substrate
claims.excerpt: Once Step 7 production starts on a judge model, that model runs through Step 8 grading. No per-cell judge selection.

claims.claim: Opus 4.7 pricing is $5/$25 input/output base (~1.67× Sonnet baseline); src/extraction/pricing.ts was staleness-fixed from $15/$75 to $5/$25 base verified 2026-04-30
claims.rationale: Pricing model anchor for cost projections; pre-amendment $100 framing was staleness-anchored
claims.excerpt: Opus 4.7 verified pricing ($5/$25 input/output base; ~1.67× Sonnet baseline pricing)

claims.claim: Per-cell n=5 is the CI-computation floor; below n=5 is embarrassingly small-N for 95% CI bounds
claims.rationale: Substrate floor rationale; full-matrix replication deferred post-v1.0
claims.excerpt: Per-cell n=5 is CI-computation floor (below = embarrassingly small-N for 95% CI bounds).

claims.claim: Position-correlation imbalance > 0.60 triggers verification (not a methodology failure); style-normalization re-grade differentiates format-based vs content-based leakage
claims.rationale: Triggering verification is by design; the post-hoc style-normalization branch determines outcome framing
claims.excerpt: Triggering the verification is NOT a methodology failure; it is a verification mechanism that runs to detect residual leakage.

claims.claim: Quality-axis gating thresholds: per-axis within-1-point agreement ≥ 80%, aggregate Spearman ≥ 0.6, per-axis direction agreement ≥ 75%, plus variance trigger thresholds at 20%/50%/100% tokens range/mean
claims.rationale: Locked threshold values per v0.5-SCOPE.md §7.1.1 + §7.3.1
claims.excerpt: Quality-axis gating thresholds (Step 6) and variance-trigger thresholds (Steps 6 + 7) lock per `v0.5-SCOPE.md` §7.1.1 + §7.3.1.

claims.claim: Range/mean (not CV) is the variance metric for cross-cycle comparability with Phase 8 §8 framing
claims.rationale: CV is more standard at n ≥ 5 but range/mean preserves comparability; persisted data allows CV recomputation
claims.excerpt: Range/mean (not CV) as variance metric for cross-cycle comparability with Phase 8 §8 framing.

claims.claim: Rubric DESIGN locks in this ADR at Step 1; rubric PROMPT TEXT commits to source (src/grading/rubric-prompt.ts) at Step 3
claims.rationale: Two-lock-point clarification per v0.5-SCOPE.md §7.2.1 separates methodology lock from prompt-text lock
claims.excerpt: rubric DESIGN locks here at Step 1; rubric PROMPT TEXT commits to source at Step 3

claims.claim: Rubric locks at this ADR; mid-cycle refinement is a rescope condition, not a routine path

claims.claim: Rubric uses 4 axes (factual correctness, completeness, actionability, hallucination) on a 0-3 ordinal scale anchored with worked examples from real Phase 5 trial outputs
claims.rationale: Four axes isolate distinct failure modes; example-anchored anchors survive peer review where aspirational ones don't
claims.excerpt: Four axes (Q2 lean confirmed; per-failure-mode separability)

claims.excerpt: Spearman (rank correlation) is chosen over Pearson (linear) — 0-3 ordinal scores have no meaningful interval scale.

claims.claim: The adapter's `workspace/configuration` handler MUST return a length-matched array (not null); returning null causes gopls to skip workspace view creation.
